introduction: On this Sunday, the readings speak of shepherds. Through Jeremiah, God condemns shepherds who scatter his flock and promises to gather it himself. In the Gospel, Jesus invites his tired apostles to rest, and he has compassion on the crowd who are like sheep without a shepherd. Paul tells us that Christ is our peace. Let us come to the Good Shepherd, who gives us rest.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is our shepherd; there is nothing we shall want. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the shepherds of the Church, our Pope, our bishop and our priests: that they may care for God's people with the compassion of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are overworked and exhausted: that they may find time to rest with the Lord. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel lost, scattered or abandoned: that the Good Shepherd may gather them and bring them home. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peace where there is division and hostility: that Christ, who broke down the dividing wall, may reconcile enemies. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may make time each day to rest in God's presence. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you had compassion on the crowds. Give rest to the weary, gather the scattered, and make us one in your peace. You live and reign for ever and ever.

reflection.title: Come away and rest
reflection.body:
Through Jeremiah, God speaks hard words to the leaders of his people: "Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!" But the reading turns to hope. God himself will gather his flock, and he promises: "I will raise to David a righteous Branch." The Church sees that promise fulfilled in Jesus.

In the Gospel, the apostles return from their mission full of news. Jesus sees how tired they are: "there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat." So he says, "Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile." Jesus cares about rest. He knows that people who serve others need time apart with him.

But the crowd gets there first. Instead of being annoyed, Jesus is moved: "he had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things." His heart goes out to people who are lost.

The psalm sings what this shepherd gives: "He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul." And Paul tells us that this shepherd gathers people who were divided: "For he is our peace, who made both one, and broke down the middle wall of separation."

Many of us live with too much coming and going and not enough rest. Jesus invites us, as he invited his apostles, to come away with him for a while. This week, find a quiet place and a quiet time, even ten minutes, to rest with the Lord. Pray Psalm 23 slowly. And ask him to show you someone who is like a sheep without a shepherd, to whom you can show his compassion.
